purpose: Separate static progenitor-compartment abundance from the susceptibility/competence of stem/progenitor systems to activate, differentiate and support follicle function.

support: Garza et al. 2011: preserved KRT15-high human AGA stem-cell compartment with marked depletion of CD200-high/ITGA6-high and CD34-high progenitor populations
Bazid et al. 2026: preserved Sox9 with reduced CD34 in frontal bald AGA scalp, including frontal-vs-occipital differences

chi_P.meaning: local activation/conversion/differentiation susceptibility of the stem/progenitor system under a declared perturbation
support: Leirós et al. 2012: in a human AGA-DPC/HFSC coculture, androgen exposure impaired hair-follicle stem-cell differentiation and Wnt/beta-catenin activation restored differentiation-related output

Wen et al. 2025: primary human HFSC experiments showed retinoic-acid-associated proliferation and changes from stemness toward progenitor/differentiation markers, attenuated by RA-receptor or Wnt-pathway blockade; miniaturized frontal AGA HFs in organ culture also showed functional growth/cycle responses
Edelkamp et al. 2026: human HF ex-vivo OR2A4/7 agonism delayed catagen and expanded CD34-positive immediate progeny and CD71-positive transit-amplifying populations alongside hair-growth promotion

non_equivalences: CD34 abundance != unique functional progenitor reserve scalar
in-vitro marker conversion != in-vivo durable regeneration
one pathway-specific rescue != universal restoration of the progenitor compartment
evidence_scope_notes: The 2012 coculture is a human cellular functional assay but does not reproduce the full in-vivo follicle niche.

The 2025 study combines human AGA organ culture, primary HFSC experiments, animal work and a clinical study; HF01 uses the human cell/organ findings here only as source-bound functional-conversion evidence, not as a treatment recommendation.
The 2026 OR2A4/7 ex-vivo study supports human progenitor/function coupling but is not promoted here as an AGA-specific recovery experiment.
None of these studies provides definitive lineage tracing from one identified human HFSC through progenitor state to durable hair recovery in vivo.
model_update: Retain P as a compartment/state coordinate, and represent activation/conversion competence as a response susceptibility chi_P rather than folding both into one scalar.
next_high_information_test: In a linked human HF system, measure baseline progenitor state and a prospectively declared activation/conversion response, then test whether chi_P adds later-function prediction beyond P_state while preserving unit identity and controlling probe back-action.
claim_ceiling: human source-bound evidence that progenitor abundance and progenitor activation/conversion response are experimentally separable and both can associate with follicle functional outputs; not a validated recoverability coordinate.
